## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks the correctness gaps only on a bare plan — completeness gaps below stay informational until a detail bundle exists.     plan-tool completeness-apply roadmap-feedback-revision-bounded-operations   # walk + apply each correctness gap

- HIGH `[baseline-migration-provenance]`: Step 4 (`Persist a writer-owned canonical non-feedback baseline with every semantic roadmap publication`) calls its first baseline a “trusted canonical copy” and says migration is never a chance to “bless the current text,” while **Risks** says it must never update from a direct edit. `roadmap.py:_load_stage_artifact` and the stage parse/render functions see only current bytes, so a hand-changed row or body value that still renders canonically is indistinguishable from an earlier writer publication and will become the first baseline; the **Architecture** migration paragraph, **Testing**, and baseline acceptance criterion leave the direct-edit refusal false at rollout.
  - Fix: define a writer-proven or explicitly approved trust boundary for first-baseline migration and align the refusal guarantee and migration tests to it.
- HIGH `[plans-publication-seed-freshness]`: Step 4 (`Persist a writer-owned canonical non-feedback baseline with every semantic roadmap publication`) makes only the artifact/baseline pair “one recoverable generation,” while step 5 (`Route every re-entered stage by active feedback, refuse unauthorized non-feedback changes, and re-gate feedback-free stages without writes`) makes a successful bounded merge the only path that invalidates derived seeds. Testing covers interruption between artifact and baseline replacement, and Acceptance covers pair recovery and feedback-free zero seed changes, but neither covers a Plans publication that commits its new artifact/baseline before seed invalidation. At HEAD, `roadmap.py:_write_artifact` and `_invalidate_roadmap_seeds` are separate writes, so this boundary can leave changed Plans content with derived seeds still marked current.
  - Fix: make Plans artifact, baseline, and seed-state freshness one recoverable publication result, with recovery that never leaves a new artifact/baseline paired with current derived seeds.
